contract.headline: A 48h timelock covers contract-upgrade (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, UPGRADER_ROLE). asset-permission (MINTER_ROLE) has NO established delay — timelock: none. The delay protects the code and not the supply.

reUSDe is the JUNIOR tranche. It absorbs losses BEFORE reUSD — that
subordination is the entire protection reUSD holders have.
Measured 2026-09-06: timelock 0x69ddea33…fca93 holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and
UPGRADER_ROLE on BOTH 0x5086bf…0c72 (senior) and 0xdDC0f880…cC5a (junior),
with 0x…dEaD false on every check as control.
Both proxies also point at the SAME implementation 0xb5276c43…21d4 (6,498B).
⚠️ So the senior/junior split is a DESIGN property, not an ENFORCED one: one
48-hour delay and one key set stand behind both sides of the subordination.
Whether that matters is riskAnalyst's call, not this file's.
